limitations: Learned participants are reference learners (~80k parameters, hashed features over schema-driven candidates), initialised by behaviour cloning on SCRIPTED demonstrations in CPU training worlds (labelled in evidence); imitation is weak (held-out tool agreement with the demonstrator 0.22 argmax) and within a few simulated days their reinforcement learning is small and mostly driven by the intrinsic novelty/rejection terms (the external drives are almost always zero in a civilisation run: no revenue arrives in 3-4 days). Measured honestly: parameter change, behaviour change on recorded situations vs frozen copy and no-signal twin, early/late action outcomes, held-out final vs initial difference (negative in the measured run).

Three argument types (code commits, contract clause lists, service inputs) use scripted syntax with learned choices; the code a participant writes comes from six utility families or wraps a package it found; free texts are composed from words it read.
Semantic generalists (class 4) take part with choice_method 'mean' (one scoring pass) for cost, one decision every 2 simulated hours; they do not update parameters.
Population class 4 rows of crucible.population are inert (label only, workstream B/D); SP-12.1's semantic kind is the harness's SemanticAgent.
Collusion detectors use pre-registered thresholds; tacit collusion without any world communication channel is not flagged as collusion.

The private-observation audit sees only what each participant receives through the experience interface; participants run in the harness's process (a learner holding a world handle would bypass it) - the structural audit checks that none does.
Gate runs need the GPU text path (Qwen3-0.6B) of the civilisation; the shared GPU slot queue was ~25-34 jobs deep during this wave.

SP-12.0 (>= 10 of 11 capability kinds by learning parties) was not reached in a measured civilisation run (7, then 8); compete_for_scarce_resources and develop_competing_technologies need two learning parties to rent at one provider / release packages of one function family within the run.
integration_notes: experience (L): KernelExperienceEnv.add_agent has no controller parameter; crucible.multiagent.harness admits through admin.join(controller=...) and adopts the principal. A controller parameter on add_agent (and on make(3, ...) agents) would let every multi-agent harness record parties.

selfplay.arena (mine): outside legacy mode SelfPlayEnv.step / KernelSelfPlayEnv.step return an empty info; operators read env.last_info (selfplay.experiments.job_kernel and selfplay.audit updated). Any external caller that read info['net_cents'] outside legacy must use last_info.

Gate tests: tests/v5/test_gate_Q.py and test_gate_SP_12_0.py run the full campaign (demonstrations ~100 s, pre-training ~200 s, held-out family ~30 s, 96 simulated hours of civilisation ~5 min, then held-out evaluation / strategy switch; ~12-20 min in a GPU slot); the SP-12.1/1b/2/3/3b files run a short campaign (24 h, 2.5-4 min). Measured peak RSS 2.5 GB, GPU < 3 GB: --cpu 1 --gpu-mb 4000 --ram-mb 6000 suffice. The manifest's tests field for SP-12.0/12.1b/12.2/12.3b already names these files.
ACCEPTANCE_MANIFEST implementation_files for Q.*/SP-12.* are empty; the files above should be synced by QA (ablation needs them).

semantic participants (D): in the self-play civilisation (576 tools) a SemanticParticipant with choice_method 'mean' picks among the BM25 top tools for its goal text; with the goal 'build a useful developer tool' those were make.build_facility / make.sell (industrial factories), all rejected, and its accepted calls were read-only (world.find_tools). The harness now words builder goals with the tools' own vocabulary (create a repo, commit, register, release); a candidate list that always contains the creating tool of each noun in the goal would make goal wording matter less.

QA: every K gate file shares tests/v5/_selfplay_kit.py (campaign set-up, sizes); ablation of any multiagent module makes every K gate fail (each file runs the whole campaign). Unofficial civilisation runs of this wave used scratch lanes; their evidence was written under $TMPDIR/crucible-v5-unofficial-evidence only.

population (B/J): the civilisation's own population did not buy from, read or engage with the learners' products, packages or posts within 72-96 simulated hours in any measured run (cooperation_with_world_parties 0); the learners' external drives were therefore almost always zero. If population demand for new developer tools/products exists in a civilisation profile, a longer run or that profile would give self-play a real revenue signal.
